title: Five cross-process 1v1 vs TagDuel acceptance lock races
priority: P1 — provar exclusão mútua real entre Accept 1v1 e Accept TagDuel sob concorrência entre processos: duas conexões SQLite independentes não podem adquirir simultaneamente os locks do mesmo jogador.

design.isolation: temporary SQLite file seeded by the parent process; parent connection closed before workers start
design.concurrency: Five independent lobbies, tested sequentially; each race uses two independent Node child processes with separate better-sqlite3 connections. Both workers signal ready and receive the same scheduled startAt.
design.invariant: exactly one acceptance and exactly one invitee lock (duel_members XOR tag_members)

assertions: five independent races each begin with both invitations pending and no invitee lock
both workers in each race start from the same scheduled timestamp
exactly one process commits its acceptance in every race
the losing transaction fails closed with a cross-mode conflict or SQLite busy error
persisted duel/lobby state agrees with the winning lock table in all five races
original host and duel-creator locks remain intact in all five races
players, player_cards, starter_grants, decks and deck_cards remain byte-equivalent before and after all races
limitations: Process-level concurrency against temporary SQLite; no production database.
Uses the real duelStore/tagStore acceptance transactions, not a live Discord gateway.
The test proves lock exclusivity; it does not claim a friendly user-facing retry message for SQLITE_BUSY.

testExecution.extendedSoak: not applicable to this test-only PR
